# Strict parity witness counts do not eliminate arbitrary circuit menus
count-only topological or colorful-selection continuation. It is NOT
an actual critical-cap construction or a below-OC minimizer. It proves
that the new strict arithmetic count and the complete abstract menu
condition are compatible, even with unusually strong regularity.

Archive inventory: the universal-over-selections condition, essential
rank lemma, and cone cover are already in
candidate 849b2bf661bcc86d and
fixed-parity-face-witnesses-and-all-circuit-protecting-cones-coherent.md.
The impossibility of freezing multipliers is already characterized in
all-critical-cover-game-and-frozen-multiplier-obstruction-coherent.md.
The new point here is an exact family SATURATING the improved rank
k-2 on actual complete lattice sets with the strict face count k-1,
while also admitting pointed protecting cones, full-dimensional
menus, and a globally continuous uniformly positive adaptive balance.
Thus continuity or an antipodal-free sphere cover does not itself
repair the remaining geometric gap.

## 1. Actual arithmetic labels with the sharp strict witness count

Fix any integer k>=3 and put s=k-1. In Z^s take

    B=conv{0,2e_1,e_2,...,e_s},
    I=B intersect Z^s={0,e_1,2e_1,e_2,...,e_s}.

The equality follows from x_j>=0 and
x_1/2+sum_(j>=2)x_j<=1. Thus |I|=k+1>k, and its occupied
parities are precisely those of 0,e_1,...,e_s. Its maximal
occupied minimal faces are

    F_1=[0,2e_1],       F_i={e_i} for 2<=i<=s.

Choose fixed witnesses p_i=e_i. There are exactly s=k-1 of them,
so the strict arithmetic theorem is attained. These are actual
lattice-complete arithmetic data. The following menus are assigned
to these fixed labels; they are not asserted to arise as derivatives
of convex-body cap budgets on that lattice set.

## 2. Full-dimensional nonzero menus and exact adaptive balance

Use the Euclidean parameter space

    E={x in R^s: sum_i x_i=0},       dim E=s-1=k-2.

Identify linear functionals on E with vectors in E, and put

    v_i=e_i-(1/s)1,
    epsilon=1/(4s),
    Gamma_i=v_i+epsilon closed_unit_ball(E).             (1)

These are compact convex FULL-DIMENSIONAL menus. None contains zero,
because |v_i|=sqrt((s-1)/s)>=1/sqrt(2)>epsilon. Their total span
is E. For EVERY independent choice g_i=v_i+d_i in Gamma_i there
is a unique probability vector pi satisfying

    sum_i pi_i g_i=0,
    2/(3s)<=pi_i<=4/(3s) for every i.                    (2)

Moreover pi depends continuously on the entire chosen menu tuple.

Here is an explicit proof. Let Delta:R^s->E have columns d_i, and
pi_0=(1/s)1. Its operator norm is at most the Frobenius norm,

    ||Delta||<=sqrt(s) epsilon<=1/4.

Write pi=pi_0+eta with eta in E. Since sum_i pi_i v_i=eta,
the balancing equation is

    (Id_E+Delta|E) eta=-Delta pi_0.

The operator is invertible by its convergent Neumann series, and
|Delta pi_0|<=epsilon. Thus the unique solution satisfies

    |eta|<=epsilon/(1-1/4)=1/(3s).

Every coordinate pi_i is therefore between 2/(3s) and 4/(3s),
proving positivity, normalization, and (2). The same inverse
formula proves continuity (indeed smooth dependence throughout a
neighborhood of the compact menu product). This is the original
quantifier order: FOR EVERY chosen cover there EXISTS its balance.
The balance has not been fixed before the independent choices.

There is no probability vector balancing all menu choices at once.
Varying just the ith g_i in its positive-radius ball and subtracting
the two alleged common identities would force pi_i=0. Doing this
for each index contradicts sum pi_i=1. The required adaptive
multipliers are nonetheless continuous and uniformly positive.

## 3. Pointed cone coverage with a quantitative strict margin

The protecting cones are exactly

    T_i={x in E:g.x>=0 for every g in Gamma_i}
       ={x in E:x_i>=epsilon |x|}.                     (3)

They are closed convex cones, and each contains no pair of opposite
nonzero vectors. Their intersection is {0}. Yet they cover E with
the uniform strict margin

    Phi(x):=max_i min_(g in Gamma_i) g.x
            >=(3/(4s)) |x|.                            (4)

To prove the estimate, let A=max_i x_i. For x!=0, zero coordinate
sum gives A>0. Define

    w_j=A1-sA e_j,
    lambda_j=(A-x_j)/(sA).

Then lambda_j>=0, sum lambda_j=1, and x=sum lambda_j w_j.
Each |w_j|=A sqrt(s(s-1)), so

    A>=|x|/sqrt(s(s-1))>=|x|/s.

Since the minimum over the ball in (1) is exactly
x_i-epsilon|x|, this proves (4). On the unit sphere of the
(k-2)-dimensional space E, the resulting s=k-1 protecting sets
are a finite closed antipodal-free cover. This is an explicit
construction, not an invocation of a conjectural selection theorem.

Every label is essential: for j!=i,
v_j.v_i=-1/s, so v_i belongs to none of the T_j with j!=i.
It does belong to T_i. Removing any witness therefore leaves a
direction unprotected. The essential-block rank is exactly

    dim span(union_i Gamma_i)=s-1=k-2.                 (5)

This saturates the newly improved rank bound. There is no zero
gradient in any menu and no nonzero common annihilating direction
in this effective parameter space. A larger parameter space can
of course be obtained by adding a common kernel; that merely
reproduces the already known rank reduction.

## 4. A finite rational menu version

The phenomenon does not require infinitely many circuit choices.
Let r=s-1 and delta=1/(8s). Replace (1) by the convex hull of the
following 2r explicitly rational response vectors at each label:

    v_i+delta(e_j-e_s),
    v_i-delta(e_j-e_s),        1<=j<=r.                  (6)

Every error vector in this polytope has Euclidean norm at most
sqrt(2)/(8s)<epsilon. Thus all of Section 2, including uniqueness,
continuous positive balances, and the numerical bounds (2), holds
for arbitrary choices in these convexified FINITE menus. They are
full-dimensional in E and exclude zero.

Their protecting cones are now polyhedral:

    T_i={x in E:x_i>=delta max_(j<=r)|x_j-x_s|}.        (7)

They still satisfy (4), since the menus are subsets of the balls.
Each cone is pointed: if both x and -x satisfy (7), then
max_j|x_j-x_s|=0, so all coordinates agree and their sum zero
forces x=0. Each label remains essential, because v_i has
v_j.v_i=-1/s<0 for j!=i and zero error is in each convexified menu.
The finite menus also have no fixed common balancing probability:
their differences span E at each label, so the same subtraction
argument forces every alleged fixed coefficient to vanish.

## 5. Exact conclusion and remaining geometric scope

For k=2, strict face compression gives one witness; its universal
signed-linear condition indeed forces Gamma_1={0}. That is a
stationarity statement, not a contradiction. For every k>=3,
Sections 1--4 show that even all of the following are compatible:

* the actual strict arithmetic configuration |I|>k and s=k-1;
* compact full-dimensional menus, with finitely many generating
  response vectors if desired, none equal to zero;
* universal positive dependence for EVERY independent menu choice;
* unique, globally continuous, uniformly positive balancing weights;
* pointed, antipodal-free protecting cones with strict directional
  protection and no redundant witness;
* the exact maximal permitted essential rank k-2.

Thus these count, menu, and topological properties alone cannot
eliminate all deepest-face menus or force a profitable direction.
They already possess the explicit models above. A numerical value
of beta can be attached to an abstract response problem without
changing them, but that would NOT make it a realized below-target
mixed-integer family.

This result does not rule out a topological argument using additional
proved identities specific to actual critical caps, their feasible
body variations, or their mass geometry at a bad minimizer. Such an
identity would be materially new input. The present obstruction
closes only the shortcut from strict witness count plus arbitrary
menus, and does not replace that missing input by an OC-equivalent
selection assumption.
